newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open flat, property stocks rally.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open flat, property stocks rally.

text.p: Singapore shares opened flat on Monday with a rebound in the property sector balancing generally weaker industrial blue chip shares, dealers said.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrial Index stood at 2,066.19 points at 0130 GMT, down just 2.29.

The Singapore property share index was up 17.36 points, or 2.54 percent at 699.55, as dealers reacted to Saturday's government announcement of curbs on loans for purchases of local public housing. The government will stop subsidising loans to Singaporeans with incomes over Singapore $8,000 ($5,555) per month and limit subsidised loans for all home buyers.
Property shares dominated early volume, taking four of the top five slots on the actives board.
Wing Tai Holdings was the most active, rising 24 cents to Singapore $4.20 on four million shares. City Developments jumped 30 cents to S$12.70. DBS Land rose 20 cents to S$5.00.
Rumours of the measures hit the market on Friday, prompting fears they could be a dampener on an already weak stock market. In the event the measures proved less draconian than feared.
Shares in local shipping company NOL failed to react to news it would acquire U.S. shipping group APL.
